reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it presents BitConnect as a way to earn cryptocurrency income through a stated 1% daily-interest technique and a projected $1,420.25 profit from a $500 investment. It directs viewers to buy at least $100 in bitcoin, send it to an address, accept terms, and pay, while showing lending, daily interest, and delayed capital release. The material does not establish a completed transaction, actual payout, or the accuracy of the claimed returns, and separate Coinbase and savings-page screens do not independently substantiate the BitConnect offer.

citations.quote: Today, a video to show you a technique to earn money passively!
you will first have to buy some bitcoin 100$ that's the minimum price
send the bitcoin get the address
Here I offer you a technique to have some interest on your daily rents, so 1% out of your daily income.
I still haven't earned anything yet because I just made my first deposit

opening.argument: The presentation is notably transparent about uncertainty and personal experience rather than promising a guaranteed result. The speaker says, “I still haven't earned anything yet because I just made my first deposit,” expressly distinguishing a recent deposit from an established payout. The language also remains tentative: the technique “can be interesting,” and the speaker says they will show withdrawal and reinvestment in another video rather than claiming that viewers have already profited. That disclosure supports treating this as conditional investment commentary, not a deceptive certification of returns.

citations.quote: I still haven't earned anything yet because I just made my first deposit
I'm sure it can be interesting to hear them
I will show you in another video how to withdraw and invest your money

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes a stated daily-interest technique and a projected figure, but those statements are presented alongside an admission that the speaker has not yet earned anything. The opening therefore does not establish a false guarantee or a claimed completed payout. Its description of a deposit procedure shows how the system is discussed, not that the speaker concealed the uncertainty surrounding the result.

citations.quote: I still haven't earned anything yet because I just made my first deposit
Here I offer you a technique to have some interest on your daily rents, so 1% out of your daily income.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The disclosure that the first deposit had not yet earned anything does not make the promotion cautious; it confirms that the promised result was unverified. The same presentation gives a specific daily-interest figure and a projected profit, then instructs viewers how to deposit bitcoin. Calling the claims a technique does not turn those return representations into neutral commentary.

citations.quote: Here I offer you a technique to have some interest on your daily rents, so 1% out of your daily income.
you will first have to buy some bitcoin 100$ that's the minimum price
It will bring 1420,25$ to our profit

opening.argument: The material is structured as an educational walkthrough of cryptocurrency concepts and account operations. It introduces different ways of earning virtual currencies, explains wallets, and then narrates steps for buying, transferring, and investing bitcoin. The speaker explicitly frames the subject as instruction, saying, “The first one is about mining,” followed by betting, fee missions, and trading, and promises more videos about these techniques. Showing a workflow and explaining terminology is consistent with an operational demonstration; it does not by itself establish that the presenter is certifying the external service or its outcome.

citations.quote: Different ways of earning virtual currencies. How to build your electronic wallet
The first one is about mining The second is betting
I'll do more videos about these techniques. in order to earn some money.
Once this done, you have Your investments and your total earned in investments

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution reads the instructional steps as solicitation, but the supplied material also shows a broad lesson covering mining, betting, wallets, and trading rather than a single unsupported assertion. Explaining how a user reaches an account and views investments is evidence of demonstration. It does not prove the presenter had received a payout, controlled the service, or guaranteed the displayed estimate.

citations.quote: Different ways of earning virtual currencies. How to build your electronic wallet
I'll do more videos about these techniques. in order to earn some money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The breadth of the introduction does not change the concrete conduct that follows. The speaker tells viewers to buy bitcoin, send it to an address, accept terms, and invest a specified amount. A tutorial can also function as a solicitation, and the walkthrough is specifically tied to earning interest and projected profit rather than merely explaining cryptocurrency technology.

citations.quote: you will first have to buy some bitcoin 100$ that's the minimum price
send the bitcoin get the address
It will bring 1420,25$ to our profit

opening.argument: At most, the evidence depicts promotion of an external online financial service and a referral-style purchasing flow, which fits ordinary commerce more closely than proof of a scam mechanism. The speaker directs viewers to links in the description and explains that bitcoin can be used as a tool, but the supplied record does not establish a downline, credential theft, or any completed transfer to the presenter. It also does not establish that the service actually paid anyone, that the quoted return was guaranteed, or that a viewer was required to recruit others. Those missing mechanisms matter before treating service promotion as scam content.

citations.quote: LINKS IN DESCRIPTION!
thanks to this website we can make money
you will first have to buy some bitcoin 100$ that's the minimum price
But we can't sell on the live-stream

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a deposit, an address, and delayed release, but those features can also describe the ordinary operation of an online financial product. Its own opening concedes that no completed transaction or actual payout is established. Without evidence of recruitment, credential capture, or a false outcome, the record supports service promotion and instructions, not a demonstrated scam mechanism.

citations.quote: send the bitcoin get the address
The capital is blocked for 291 days
I still haven't earned anything yet because I just made my first deposit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing mechanisms listed by the defense are not required for this category. The evidence shows the speaker promoting a deposit-based return arrangement, quoting daily interest and a projected profit, and giving viewers the minimum bitcoin purchase and transfer steps. The absence of a completed payout or recruitment scheme does not negate the solicitation of money into the described investment pool.
